statement.p: Find the velocity \vec{v}(t) and the speed \|\vec{v}(t)\| of a particle with position x = 5t^{2}-30t+45,\quad y = 6,\quad z = 4t^{3}-18t^{2}.
Find any times at which the particle stops.

p.em: (Give your answer as a time or list of times, comma separated.)

static.solution: \vec{v} is given by: \vec{v} = \frac{d}{dt}(5t^{2}-30t+45)\vec i+\frac{d}{dt}(6)\vec j+ \frac{d}{dt}(4t^{3}-18t^{2})\vec k = (10\mathopen{}\left(t-3\right))\,\vec i + (0)\,\vec j + (12t\mathopen{}\left(t-3\right))\,\vec k. The speed is given by: \|\vec v\|=\sqrt{(10\mathopen{}\left(t-3\right))^{2} + (0)^{2} + (12t\mathopen{}\left(t-3\right))^2} = 2|t - 3|\sqrt{ 25 + 36 t^2}. The particle stops when \vec v = \vec 0, so when t = 3. Since this is the only time when all components of the velocity are zero, it is the only time that the particle stops.
